specification.objective: Implement a deterministic, local task search shared by project Backlog and Kanban, using the selected project's already-loaded authorized board data and preserving existing board behavior outside the search presentation.

requirements.statement: One query state is owned by ProjectKanbanPage, remains active when switching between Backlog and Kanban, and is cleared or safely re-evaluated when the selected project changes.

A small pure Dart query interpreter normalizes case, accents, whitespace and predictable Portuguese connector words; recognizes existing task types, explicit type:bug syntax, matching status names from the current board, #number, and remaining text terms; unknown or ambiguous terms remain text rather than silently applying unsupported filters.

The query evaluator matches the same card IDs in both views using task type, current-board column ID, card number, and text in title or description, with text matching case-insensitively and accent-insensitively.
Backlog combines shared-query matches with its existing manual query/status/assignee/column filters, sorting, pagination, hierarchy, and card actions.
Kanban retains every column and card in its original order and keeps drag-and-drop behavior; active query matches are highlighted accessibly without making non-matches illegible.
Both views expose a comprehensible match count, applied criteria, empty-result state, and an accessible way to clear the shared query; no query or task data is sent to an external service or logged.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Unit tests show plain text, #number, recognized task types, explicit type:bug, dynamic current-board statuses, accent/case normalization, connector handling, and unknown/ambiguous terms produce deterministic query criteria and matches.
Widget tests verify the shared query survives view switching, does not reuse a prior project's column ID, and clearing restores the unfiltered result set.
Backlog query results compose with existing manual filters and retain sorting, paging, hierarchy and actions; query matching covers title and description and #number.

Kanban tests verify query matches are highlighted, non-matching cards remain legible, card/column counts and order are unchanged, and drag-and-drop callback behavior remains available with a query active.
Both views display an accessible count and criteria and provide a clear-query action and understandable zero-results state.

invariants.statement: Search is read-only: it does not mutate tasks, columns, persisted order, permissions, or server state.
Status recognition uses only current project column IDs/names and never assumes universal status names.
The same interpreter and evaluator determine shared-query matches in both views; Backlog-only manual filters remain local to Backlog.
Search uses only already-loaded, authorized task data and makes no network or external-service calls.

forbidden_states.statement: Kanban search removes or reorders cards/columns or changes drag-and-drop behavior.
A hard-coded global status list, untested synonym, or uncertain parse silently hides cards.
Backlog manual filters, sorting, pagination, hierarchy, or task actions regress when shared search is active.
Search sends task descriptions or queries externally, adds an external dependency, or changes backend/API/database behavior.

inputs.statement: ProjectKanbanPage shares one KanbanBoard between ProjectBacklogView and ProjectKanbanBoard; Backlog currently owns its own title/# search and filter state.

outputs.statement: A pure Dart task search interpreter/evaluator and unit tests.
A shared query control and criteria/result state in ProjectKanbanPage integrated with Backlog and Kanban presentation.
Regression tests covering parsing, match consistency, project/view transitions, preservation of Backlog controls, and Kanban order/drag behavior.

failure_semantics.statement: The focused regression test command fails on the immutable baseline because the new task-search implementation is absent and passes on the completed target.
A failing test, analyzer error, or Flutter compile/layout failure is not accepted as proof of a passing regression; preserve the exact Red probe and fix the implementation or test defect.
Ambiguous/unrecognized query fragments fall back to literal text matching instead of applying an inferred type or status filter.
